system.name: LemonNFV
system.one_liner: a framework that consolidates heterogeneous network functions into one line-rate binary and lets their per-flow state migrate freely between cores

content.subject: how a new NIC rule migrates one packet class's traffic and LEMON state from core C1 to C2

content.key_idea: One new NIC rule can hand a packet class's traffic to another core, and because code and state both live inside the LEMON binary, relocating execution is itself the state migration.

evidence: Figure 5 shows a simple migration scenario, where the operator allocates two cores
LemonNFV will create three LEMONs (M1–M3) dedicated for P1–P3
Assume we want to migrate P2 to C2.

summary: This figure illustrates LemonNFV's intra-server migration mechanism, which relocates a packet class's traffic and NF state between cores without any dedicated migration interface. Two cores, C1 and C2, each run LEMON instances dedicated to specific packet classes: M1 for P1, M2 for P2, and M3 for P3. The numbered walkthrough shows migrating packet class P2 from C1 to C2: (1) the hypervisor issues a new steering rule to the NIC redirecting P2's queue, (2) P2 is now handled by C2, (3) C1 stops seeing P2 traffic, and (4) C2 executes LEMON M2, so P2's state effectively moves with it. Because both executable code and state live inside the LEMON binary, relocating where it runs is equivalent to migrating the packet class's state, letting LemonNFV rebalance load across cores cheaply.
summary_zh: 该图展示LemonNFV的核间迁移机制：NIC下发新规则后，数据包类P2从核C1改由C2处理，其对应的LEMON实例M2随之在C2执行，代码与状态一体迁移，实现负载再平衡。
